newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African 1996/97 sugar exports 55 percent shipped.
newsitem.headline: S.African 1996/97 sugar exports 55 percent shipped.

text.p: South Africa has sold virtually all this season's sugar export surplus of around one million tonnes and more than 500,000 tonnes has already been shipped, the South African Sugar Asociation said on Wednesday.
A spokesman said over 90 percent of the season's expected exports had been committed, and around 55 percent shipped.
This year's production is estimated at 2.37 million tonnes -- the best crop in 12 years -- against 1.67 million last year, following excellent summer rains.
With domestic consumption totalling around 1.3 million tonnes, that leaves 1.0-1.1 million tonnes for export, nearly three times the 380,271 tonnes exported in 1995/96.

The principal markets remain in the Far East where South Africa has traditional long-term commitments with Japan and South Korea. Shipments to Japan this season total around 250,000 tonnes, the spokesman said.
But South Africa is also diversifying its exports this season with sales to Canada, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines and China, in addition to the U.S. where South Africa has an import quota.
Within Africa, the Sugar Association has also signed a deal with soft drink manufacturer Coca Cola to supply refined sugar to the company's East African bottling operations.
